forms.name: Resin Art
forms.description: Pouring liquid epoxy resin mixed with pigments to create glossy, glass-like fluid art and functional items.

forms.name: Punch Needle & Tufting
forms.description: Modern textile arts using specialized needles to loop yarn into thick, plush rugs and wall decor.

forms.name: Alcohol Ink Art
forms.description: Creating vibrant, ethereal abstract designs by manipulating fast-drying dye inks on non-porous surfaces.

forms.name: Fluid Acrylic Pouring
forms.description: Thinning acrylic paints with mediums to pour and tilt them across canvases, creating marbled patterns.

forms.name: Digital Painting & Concept Art
forms.description: Using drawing tablets and software to create hyper-detailed visual art, illustrations, and animations.

forms.name: 3D Pen Sculpting
forms.description: Extruding heated plastic filament that instantly cools to draw three-dimensional sculptures in mid-air.

forms.name: Eco-Printing
forms.description: Steaming or boiling leaves and flowers bundled tightly against fabric to transfer their natural pigments directly.

forms.name: Upcycled & Mixed Media Assemblage
forms.description: Combining discarded objects, scrap metals, and different mediums into cohesive modern sculptures.

forms.name: Paper Quilling
forms.description: Rolling, shaping, and gluing narrow paper strips together to create intricate, 3D mosaic-like designs.

forms.name: Origami
forms.description: The traditional Japanese art of folding flat paper sheets into complex geometric shapes and objects without cutting.

forms.name: Modern Faux Calligraphy & Hand Lettering
forms.description: Stylizing text by drawing fake brush strokes, heavily popularized in modern graphic design.

forms.name: Decoupage
forms.description: Gluing printed paper cutouts onto home goods, furniture, or frames and sealing them with thick lacquer.

forms.name: Papier-Mâché
forms.description: Building lightweight, durable objects and masks out of paper pulp or paper strips mixed with paste.

forms.name: Scherenschnitte
forms.description: Highly intricate traditional German paper-cutting that uses fine scissors to create symmetrical silhouettes.

forms.name: Studio Ceramics
forms.description: Modern wheel-throwing and hand-building techniques used to create unique, contemporary functional pottery.

forms.name: Kintsugi
forms.description: The Japanese art of repairing broken pottery with lacquer dusted with real gold, highlighting flaws instead of hiding them.

forms.name: Murano Glassblowing
forms.description: The famous Venetian tradition of shaping molten glass into colorful, fluid sculptures and vessels.

forms.name: Stained Glass
forms.description: Creating large windows or panels by arranging colored glass pieces held together with lead framing.

forms.name: Azulejos
forms.description: Distinctive, historically blue-and-white tin-glazed ceramic tiles characteristic of Portuguese architecture.

forms.name: Celadon Pottery
forms.description: Jade-green glazed stoneware highly valued across East Asia for its smooth finish and subtle cracks.

forms.name: Oil Painting
forms.description: Classic European canvas mastery utilizing slow-drying pigments, refined heavily during the Renaissance.

forms.name: Chinese Shanshui
forms.description: Traditional brush-and-ink landscape paintings executed on delicate silk or paper scrolls.

forms.name: Ukiyo-e
forms.description: Japanese woodblock prints that captured urban pop culture and natural landscapes during the Edo period.

forms.name: Aboriginal Dot Painting
forms.description: Australian Indigenous storytelling using layered dots to represent land maps and sacred cultural symbols.

forms.name: Fresco Painting
forms.description: Applying water-based pigments directly onto fresh, wet lime plaster walls for permanent murals.

forms.name: Encaustic Painting
forms.description: An ancient Egyptian technique using heated, colored beeswax to paint luminous, durable portraits.

forms.name: Madhubani Painting
forms.description: Intricate, geometric folk art made with twigs, fingers, and natural dyes from Bihar.

forms.name: Warli Art
forms.description: Minimalist geometric tribal paintings from Maharashtra using circles, triangles, and squares to show village life.

forms.name: Gond Art
forms.description: Vibrant tribal paintings from Madhya Pradesh featuring dense patterns of repetitive lines and dots.

forms.name: Kalamkari
forms.description: Hand-painted or block-printed cotton textiles using natural organic dyes, native to South India.

forms.name: Pattachitra
forms.description: Highly detailed cloth-based scroll paintings depicting epic mythological tales from Odisha.

forms.name: Tanjore Painting
forms.description: Classical South Indian art heavily encrusted with genuine gold foil, semiprecious stones, and glass.

forms.name: Batik
forms.description: The Indonesian craft of applying wax-resist patterns to cloth before immersion dyeing.

forms.name: Ikat
forms.description: A highly complex resist-dyeing process applied directly to individual yarns before they are woven into fabric.

forms.name: Sashiko
forms.description: Japanese functional embroidery that uses simple running stitches to reinforce and beautifully patch old fabric.

forms.name: Macramé
forms.description: Textile work created by knotting cords together into geometric patterns, popular in bohemian home decor.

forms.name: Chikankari
forms.description: Delicate, intricate white-on-white shadow-work hand embroidery originating from Lucknow.

forms.name: Tapestry Weaving
forms.description: Heavy, hand-woven pictorial textiles designed to be hung as insulation and decoration on walls.

forms.name: Dokra
forms.description: An ancient Indian tribal lost-wax casting technique used to create detailed bronze artifacts.

forms.name: Damascening
forms.description: The luxury art of inlaying gold or silver wire into hard iron or steel surfaces.

forms.name: Filigree
forms.description: Delicate jewelry making that involves twisting and soldering fine threads of precious metals.

forms.name: Pietra Dura
forms.description: Inlaying highly polished, colored semiprecious stones into marble surfaces to form seamless images.

forms.name: Wood Carving
forms.description: Sculpting ornaments, relief scenes, or three-dimensional figures out of solid wood blocks.

forms.name: Cloisonné
forms.description: An enameling technique where wire outlines are fixed to metal surfaces and filled with colorful glass paste.

forms.name: Huichol Beadwork
forms.description: Mexican yarn and glass bead art applied over wax-coated sculptures to depict sacred visions.

forms.name: Pysanka
forms.description: Ukrainian Easter eggs decorated with highly symbolic, intricate wax-resist batik designs.

forms.name: Alebrijes
forms.description: Whimsical, brightly colored Mexican folk-art sculptures depicting fantastical, hybrid creatures.

forms.name: Totem Pole Carving
forms.description: Pacific Northwest Indigenous monumental pillars carved from massive cedar logs to display family lineages.
